question: In relation to clopidogrel, it is false that:

options.opa: It is structurally related to thienopyridines.
options.opb: It inhibits adenyl cyclase, and therefore increases cAMP levels.
options.opc: It has a low index of myelotoxicity in relation to ticlopidine.
options.opd: It has a longer action in relation to ticlopidine.
options.ope: In case of surgical intervention, it is recommended to interrupt the treatment at least one week in advance.

analysis: Clopidogrel is indeed a thienopyridine derivative (option opa is true). It does not inhibit adenyl cyclase; rather, it inhibits platelet aggregation by blocking the P2Y12 receptor (option opb is false). Clopidogrel has a lower incidence of myelotoxicity compared to ticlopidine (option opc is true). Clopidogrel has a longer duration of action than ticlopidine (option opd is true). It is generally recommended to interrupt clopidogrel treatment at least 5-7 days before surgery (option ope is true). Therefore, the false statement is option opb.
